options.text: Less than the exact value, because the rule always misses area under a rising curve.
options.why: Uses the fact that the curve is increasing instead of its concavity to decide the direction of the error.

options.why: Assumes equal strip widths guarantee exactness. They do not; although straight lines give exact estimates, nonlinear functions can also have cancelling errors.

questions.solution_text:
$y=2^{x}$ is an exponential growth curve, so it is concave up on $0\le x\le 3$.
Every chord joining two points of a concave-up curve lies above the curve.
Each trapezium therefore includes extra area, so the estimate is greater than the exact value.

Greater than the exact value, because the curve is concave down so every chord lies above it.
options.why: Correct concavity but the chord is placed on the wrong side of a concave-down curve.

options.text: Greater than the exact value, because the trapezia bulge outwards near the maximum at $x=3$.
options.why: Reads the shape of the graph near its turning point instead of applying the concavity rule.

options.text: Equal to the exact value, because the interval is symmetric about the turning point.
options.why: Assumes symmetry makes the rule exact; symmetry does not remove the gap between a chord and a curve.

questions.solution_text:
$y=6x-x^{2}$
$y'=6-2x$
$y''=-2$
$y''<0$, so the curve is concave down on $1\le x\le 5$.
Every chord lies below the curve, so the estimate is less than the exact value.

questions.question_text:
A vertical rock cutting is $240$ metres long. Its heights, in metres, are measured at $40$-metre intervals along a straight horizontal base.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}x&0&40&80&120&160&200&240\\\hline \text{height}&4&9&12&15&10&6&2\end{array}$
Use the Trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the cutting.

options.why: Doubled the endpoint heights as well as the interior heights, giving $40(4+9+12+15+10+6+2)$.
Counted every height only once, giving $20(4+9+12+15+10+6+2)$.
Used $h=40$ instead of $\frac{h}{2}=20$ as the multiplier, doubling the estimate.

questions.question_text:
The Trapezoidal rule with $4$ strips is used to estimate the signed integral $\int_{0}^{2}\left(x^{2}-5\right)dx$.
How does the estimate compare with the exact value of this integral?

options.text: Greater than the exact value, because the curve is concave up and the chords lie above it.
Less than the exact value, because a concave-up curve has chords below it.
options.why: Reverses the position of the chords for a concave-up curve.

options.text: Less than the exact value, because the graph lies below the $x$-axis.
options.why: Confuses the signed integral with unsigned area; chords above a negative graph give a greater, less negative integral estimate.

options.text: Equal to the exact value, because the strips have equal widths.
options.why: Assumes equal strip widths guarantee exactness, ignoring the gaps between the chords and this curved graph.

questions.solution_text:
$y=x^{2}-5$ has $y''=2>0$, so it is concave up on $0\le x\le2$.
The chords lie above the curve, so the trapezoidal estimate of the signed integral is greater than its exact value.
The graph is below the $x$-axis throughout this interval, so both values are negative and the estimate is less negative; the corresponding unsigned area estimate is smaller than the true area.
